questions.title: The Golgi apparatus's defining structural feature
questions.question: Which of the following structural features is uniquely characteristic of the Golgi apparatus?

options.C: Composed of large and small functional subunits
options.D: Outer smooth and inner rough cellular membranes

explanations.A: Incorrect. Janus Green is the classic supravital stain for MITOCHONDRIA, not the Golgi apparatus.
explanations.B: Correct. The Golgi apparatus is structurally a stack of flat saccules with an entry (cis) and an exit (trans) face; everything the Golgi packages and buds off leaves from the exit face. This stacked-saccule architecture is the feature that structurally distinguishes it from other membranous organelles.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Large and small subunits describe the RIBOSOME (large and small ribosomal subunits), not the Golgi apparatus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. An outer smooth, inner rough membrane arrangement describes the nuclear envelope (whose outer membrane is continuous with rough ER), not the Golgi apparatus.

questions.learning_objective: Name the stack of flat saccules with entry and exit faces as the Golgi apparatus's defining EM structure.
